result.concerns:
1) SR-play-app-7 deviation: the 16 KB rule is enforced for 64-bit ABIs only (arm64-v8a, x86_64); 32-bit libraries are parsed but exempt because 16 KB page-size devices run 64-bit code only. Enforcing it on armeabi-v7a/x86 would risk false CI failures for a non-requirement. No real AAB could be built here (no Android SDK), so the check has not yet run against the actual graphics-path libraries; if a 64-bit .so in the bundle is 4 KB aligned the next CI run will fail, which is the intended signal.
2) SR-play-app-2 choices: the signing job is workflow_dispatch-only (no `tags: v*` trigger) so the reviewed push-trigger policy in the lock stays unchanged; the owner dispatches on the release ref with -f sign_release=true. Unsigned artifact upload is skipped on pull_request to bound artifact storage on a private repo. The upload-artifact SHA (v5.0.0 = 330a01c490aca151604b8cf639adc76d48f6c5d4) was read via `git ls-remote` through the proxy because the GitHub API was blocked for this session; the owner should confirm it against the release page before relying on it. The lock's verifiedAt was bumped to 2026-10-25. The release-sign job and the new lintRelease tasks are static only: no runner/SDK here, so the first real run may surface lint findings on wear (warningsAsErrors) that the plan accepted as a risk.
3) SR-play-app-3: the Wear versionCode jumps from 1 to 1000035; it was never uploaded to Play and any sideloaded Wear install sees an increase. The Companion line (im.binario.companion, codes 3/4) is untouched. Owner action unchanged: never pass -PBINARIO_VERSION_CODE for a Play upload; bump BINARIO_APP_VERSION_CODE per release.
4) SR-play-app-5: the 'No collection/sharing' Data safety answer is a documented judgment (user-initiated, ephemeral request of a public station id to RFI; no developer backend); a conservative alternative declaration is written down for the owner/reviewer. The public privacy-policy URL remains a pre-existing blocker. The new host guard means any http(s) host added to app/wear Kotlin or the asset manifests now fails verify_privacy_policy.py until the table is updated (intended).
5) SR-play-app-4: the Play icon derives from companion-expo/assets/brand/binario-companion-icon.png, which is the same teal (#005A52) train mark as the app's ic_binario vector and fully opaque (verified). Listing texts and release notes are proposals in five languages; the owner must still produce the feature graphic and screenshots and confirm the 12-tester/14-day closed-testing rule in the Console, as Play thresholds change.
6) CHANGELOG.md was not updated, matching the other fix commits on this branch. The kt/android-check.sh harness named in the task does not exist in the scratchpad (only mariadb-up.sh), but no Kotlin source was changed, only wear/build.gradle.kts.

findings.description: test_wear_version_code_is_derived_from_the_phone_code_in_a_disjoint_range hard-codes the literal "BINARIO_APP_VERSION_CODE=35\n" in two replacing() mutations. The very owner action this branch documents for every release (bump BINARIO_APP_VERSION_CODE in gradle.properties) therefore turns the regression suite red with a misleading message. Verified in a scratch copy: with BINARIO_APP_VERSION_CODE=36 the verifier itself prints PASS but `python3 -m unittest tests.test_verify_android_release_config` fails with `AssertionError: BINARIO_APP_VERSION_CODE=35` coming from the `assert old in text` guard. The package's own gate is `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`, so the next release breaks it.
findings.suggested_fix:
Derive the current line instead of hard-coding it, e.g. `current = re.search(r"^BINARIO_APP_VERSION_CODE=\d+
", POLICY.read("gradle.properties"), re.M).group(0)` and use `replacing("gradle.properties", current, current + "BINARIO_WEAR_VERSION_CODE=35
")` and `replacing("gradle.properties", current, f"BINARIO_APP_VERSION_CODE={POLICY.WEAR_VERSION_CODE_OFFSET}
")`. Re-run the suite with a temporarily bumped code to confirm it stays green.

findings.description: test_committed_play_icon_and_readme_match_the_generator asserts byte identity between the committed store/play/icon-512.png and a fresh zlib.compress(raw, 9) output. The compressed stream is deterministic only for one zlib implementation; Python builds linked against zlib-ng or a different zlib release can emit a different stream for the same pixels, so the test can fail on another machine even though the icon is unchanged. (Local check: Python 3.11.17 / zlib 1.3 here; CI pins Python 3.12.10 on ubuntu-24.04.)
findings.suggested_fix: Compare decoded content rather than bytes: `self.assertEqual(BUILDER.read_png(committed), BUILDER.read_png(icon))` (width, height, channels, pixels) plus the README text equality; keep the size/colour assertions on the decoded pixels.

findings.description: The README text embedded in the generator (and the committed store/play/README.md) says the icon is "PNG 512×512 a 32 bit", but write_png emits colour type 2, i.e. a 24-bit RGB PNG without alpha (verified from the IHDR of the committed file: (512, 512, 8, 2, 0, 0, 0)). Play accepts both, so this is a documentation/artifact mismatch, not a submission blocker.
findings.suggested_fix: Either state "PNG RGB a 24 bit, senza trasparenza" in the README template, or emit RGBA with an opaque alpha channel (channels=4, COLOR_TYPE 6) so the text matches Google's wording.

findings.description: The new sentence "L'unica eccezione lint ammessa è `OldTargetApi`" is inaccurate: app/build.gradle.kts also carries `disable += "GradleDependency"` (lint block line 98) and wear/build.gradle.kts has six `//noinspection GradleDependency` suppressions, all policed by tests/test_wear_compose_gradle_dependency_suppressions.py.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword to: "Le sole eccezioni lint ammesse sono `OldTargetApi` (identica nei due moduli) e la policy `GradleDependency` documentata e verificata da `tests/test_wear_compose_gradle_dependency_suppressions.py`".

findings.description: The `wear_version_code > MAX_PLAY_VERSION_CODE` branch is unreachable: the preceding check forces app_version_code < 1_000_000, so the derived Wear code is at most 1_999_999. Harmless dead code.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the branch and the constant, or turn it into a comment stating the derived maximum.

findings.description: The new tests tests/test_verify_android_release_config.py, tests/test_build_store_assets.py and tests/test_play_store_docs.py run in no workflow: gtfs-assets-ci.yml and apple-watch-ci.yml list test modules explicitly and android-ci.yml runs only the Wear suppression module. Drift between the generator and store/play/*, or between the Console limits and the listing texts, is caught only locally.
findings.suggested_fix: Append the three modules to the "Offline pipeline tests" invocation in gtfs-assets-ci.yml (its path filters already include tools/** and tests/**); no lock change needed.

findings.description: actions/upload-artifact v4+/v5 refuses a second artifact with the same name inside one workflow run. If the android job uploads binario-play-bundles-unsigned and a later step fails (e.g. the reproducibility rebuild), "Re-run failed jobs" re-executes the upload step and fails with a name conflict, forcing a full re-run.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `overwrite: true` to both upload-artifact steps (verify_ci_pinning's retention/if-no-files-found checks are unaffected), or accept and document the full re-run.

result.notes: The approach is sound for all eight items and every colleague claim I could check holds (test counts, verifier output, red checks, the upload-artifact SHA the colleague asked the owner to confirm, and the Data-safety host classification). The single major finding is a self-inflicted trap in the new tests/test_verify_android_release_config.py: it hard-codes `BINARIO_APP_VERSION_CODE=35`, so the per-release bump that docs/RELEASE_BUILD.md and docs/store/PLAY_SUBMISSION.md now mandate turns the package's own gate (`python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`) red with a misleading assertion. The fix is three lines and should land as a `test(release): ...` commit on this branch. Everything else is advisory. Documented deviations I accept: the 16 KB rule applied to arm64-v8a/x86_64 only (correct for Play, 16 KB devices are 64-bit only; 32-bit ELF is still parsed fail-closed); release-sign on workflow_dispatch only instead of also `tags: v*` (keeps the reviewed trigger policy in the lock unchanged); unsigned artifacts skipped on pull_request. Static-only items by nature: Gradle lintRelease on both modules, the release-sign job, and the Wear versionCode evaluation (no SDK/runner here; the ELF check has not yet seen a real AAB, so the first CI run is the real signal, as the colleague says). Nit not worth a finding: in PLAY_DATA_SAFETY.md the "Dove nel codice" cell for jbb.ghsq.de names RemoteGtfsFallbackDataSource.kt and GtfsArtifactDownloader.kt, which hold no literal of the host (it comes from InternationalSourceCatalog.kt and EuropeanSleeperGtfsRealtimeAdapter.kt); the runtime description is right.
